subject: ventures/mini-golf-course-profit-calculator
professional: a lender-side commercial credit analyst or a small-attraction (family entertainment center) operator/consultant who writes pro formas for SBA-style build loans; first checks: level-payment loan maths, DSCR definition, whether NOI includes a replacement reserve, and whether seasonality and rain are modelled sensibly

evidence.correctness: Ran compute(SAMPLE) in node and recomputed the whole sample in an independent Python script (not the author's code). Rounds 14,094 (88/88/35 days x 0.9 open x 115/55/20), round revenue $148,788, total revenue $221,364, operating income $48,098.10, all match to the cent. Loan payment: author formula gives $34,127.16; independently verified by amortising $283,400 at 8.5% for 15 years year by year and getting a balance of ~0 after 15 payments (the standard level-payment annuity). DSCR 1.4094 = 48,098.10/34,127.16, equity payback 152,600/13,970.94 = 10.92 y, whole-investment payback 436,000/48,098.10 = 9.06 y: all match. Break-even rounds per open day solved by bisection on cash flow in Python: scale 0.92001 -> 68.28 rounds/day, identical to the tool's 68.2816. Not scored 4: no cross-check against an external published tool or lender template.
evidence.completeness: README and VENTURE claims checked against calc.mjs output: build cost per hole and shared cost (works), seasonal rounds and price (works), parties, concessions, staff, fixed costs, upkeep reserve, rain-out, loan (all in run()), operating income, DSCR, cash after loan, payback on whole investment and own money, break-even rounds/day, price change for payback target (targetPriceScale), price-by-attendance grid (5x5), weather table (rainSweep 0-30%), summary text and CSV export: all present and exercised by the 31 tests. Page markup for usage events, disclaimer and FAQ verified by page.test.mjs. No stubs or TODOs found. Stage is still 'prototype' and the hypothesis is untested, but every stated feature works.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/mini-golf-course-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 31 tests, 31 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation 1: labor computed on all season days instead of open days (ignores rain): 5 tests failed (sample P&L, loan/coverage/payback, zero-rate loan, wet-year warning, currency parsing). Seeded mutation 2: upkeep reserve base changed from build cost to total investment: the same 5 tests failed. Both reverted with git checkout; git status clean for the venture. Tests are pinned to hand-computed sample values, which is strong, but concentrated in the sample scenario, so the 5 failures show the same cluster rather than independent coverage of break-even/price-solver paths.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (all), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.test.mjs, index.html head and scripts. calc.mjs is a clean pure-function module with one run() engine reused for the base case, volume sweep, grid and weather table (no copied engines), input validation that rejects instead of clamping, null for undefined ratios. Defects: parse() uses opt() defaults so a blank loan term silently becomes 15 and blank target 8; seasons with 0 days skip rounds validation by design; the labor model is flat per open day regardless of volume (stated on page). Minor: findings text hard-codes 'about 20%' lookup via rainSweep.find(rain===20), fine. No dead code found.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'no network calls' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/WebSocket and local-only imports; passes), disclaimer 'No warranty ... not legal, tax, accounting ... advice' (index.html:143, test-backed), 'example figures illustrative' (index.html and test), DSCR threshold not asserted as a rule (finding text says lenders 'usually want 1.2 to 1.3 or more; ask yours', hedged), sponsor link and MIT LICENSE present. Backed-by-file failures: (1) sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs ('./index.html', 'Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml'); the sitemap protocol and robots.txt require absolute URLs, so crawlers will ignore them, and the test only matches /index\.html/. (2) <link rel=canonical href=./index.html> is relative. (3) llms.txt links to https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/mini-golf-course-profit-calculator/, the retired GitHub Pages address, while README/VENTURE give https://marisstella.app/...; llms.txt is stale. (4) README test command 'node --test ventures/.../**/*.test.mjs' relies on a glob and does not match files at the venture root in some shells. These are SEO/distribution claims that do not work as stated.
evidence.fitness: Walked a first-time operator's job: enter 18 holes at $12k + $220k shared, seasonal rounds/prices, a 65% loan; get NOI $48,098, DSCR 1.41, own-money payback 10.9 y vs 8-y target with 'prices ~3.5% higher' and a peak-season concentration warning, break-even 68 rounds/day vs 74 planned, weather table. That answers the 'does it pay back and how bad can a wet year get' job and shows downside in grid form. Gaps: no ramp-up year, no construction-overrun or contingency input, no income tax/depreciation (declared out of scope), no per-season staffing hours.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard FEC/attraction pro forma and commercial-lending practice: level annual payment (annual, not monthly, compounding slightly differs from a monthly-amortising lender quote), DSCR = NOI / debt service with the NOI taken after a replacement reserve (conservative, in line with lender underwriting), payback on equity using post-debt cash flow, break-even by attendance with fixed vs variable separated. Departures a credit analyst would flag: annual rather than monthly amortisation understates the payment slightly versus a real loan; flat haircut weather (stated on page) instead of a distribution; parties not reduced by rain; no year-1 ramp or working-capital/seasonal-cash-trough line; no owner's wage line (NOI before owner pay, though staff hours input can absorb it). Treated as stated limits.

defects.what: sitemap.xml and robots.txt use relative URLs (./index.html, Sitemap: ./sitemap.xml) and the canonical link is relative, so search engines will ignore them; the page test only checks the string index.html
llms.txt links to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/mini-golf-course-profit-calculator/
Loan payment uses annual compounding; a lender quotes monthly payments, so the real payment and DSCR differ slightly (about 1 to 2 percent on the sample)
README test command uses a ** glob that does not match the venture's root-level test files in sh; the working command is node --test '*.test.mjs' from the venture directory
Blank loan term and target payback silently default to 15 and 8 years instead of being flagged

verdict: The arithmetic is right and well tested: I recomputed revenue, operating income, the loan payment (by amortising to zero), DSCR, both paybacks and break-even rounds per day in an independent Python script and all matched to the cent; 31 of 31 tests pass and two seeded bugs in core logic each failed 5 tests. The page is honest about limits and carries the disclaimer, and a lender-minded reader would accept the method with its stated simplifications (annual amortisation, flat rain haircut, no ramp year). What keeps claims below the bar is distribution plumbing that does not work as stated: relative sitemap/robots/canonical URLs and a stale llms.txt address on the retired host. Meets the bar by the computed rule only if claims is 3; at claims 2 it does not meet the bar, though it is finished. The small fix is to make sitemap, robots, canonical and llms.txt absolute marisstella.app URLs and tighten the page test.
